what: New, the ＋: the one way a thing gets in. The ink button grows into a circle of the brand's field that covers the screen, and its three jobs rise out of it, centered. spec/pages.md §6.4, spec/ways-out.md §6.4.

frame.who: Every seller, many times a week; Clearing out most (a pile, fast), Testing the water (What's it worth), the hunter (Find or buy it).
frame.came_to: Say which job this thing is for in one tap, then point the camera at it, or type it when it is not at hand.
frame.costly_mistake: Picking the wrong job and losing the shots: the camera switches between Sell, Worth and Find without losing them, and × always returns the way it came.
frame.ways_out: Every job can start from words or a pasted link instead of the camera, from the pencil at its end; photos already taken come in from the camera's library button.
frame.in_the_loop: Nothing here acts for the person: every choice is theirs; words or a link become a draft they review, never a post.

decisions: The circle grows in the brand's field, sky, mint and lime, which flows over the whole screen as it grows (Ben, 06:19: "the background might be good to have that be the gradient so it can kind of almost like flow over the whole thing"). It is the field and not the wash: the wash marks the top of a main tab (U8), and the field is the one full ground a view may have (C2). In dark it is deep sky, mint and aqua, the quiet ground of the dark Today, so no light circle flashes at night.

The three jobs stand centered between the top of the screen and the × (Ben, 06:19: "center the main action buttons"), each name centered in its capsule. The last used sits lowest, nearest the ×, so the thumb's shortest reach is the likeliest job; it rises first and its icon well is the one ink circle (one emphasis per view).

＋ holds three jobs, in Ben's words: Sell it, What's it worth, Find or buy it (06:19). Everything else ＋ could start is a branch of one of them, so it is not a door of its own: cross-listing a listing already on Depop is Sell it with that listing's link pasted (Ben, 05:47); watching for a thing nobody sells yet is where Find or buy it ends when nothing matches (the want); a pile is one Sell it session per thing; linking a site lives in You.

A link or words are a way into each job, not a job (Ben, 06:19: "I don't know really what paste a link or describe it are ... They should kind of be integrated in other things"). The pencil at each job's end opens that job with one field that takes either; a link is told from words by its shape, so the person never picks which.
Each way into a job ends where the camera's way ends: Sell it at the draft's review, What's it worth on the value page for the product the words name, Find or buy it on the matches.

Capsules are 88 tall with a 56 icon well: 88 less 2 × 16 padding is 56, so the well's corner nests in the capsule's (Art. 9.1). The pencil is the kit's 40 circle with a 44 reach, in the wells' quiet gray.
Choosing a job opens the camera out of the touched capsule's icon well, on the camera's black, so the camera comes from what the finger touched (E24), in 300 ms.
A link or words can arrive from outside (a share sheet): ?link= opens Sell it with the link in its field, ?what= prefills the field of the job ?sheet= names.

Words are read with spelling tolerance, and the product they name shows under them, spelled the catalog's way ("carhart detroit" reads Carhartt Detroit Jacket J97), so a typo never reaches a title or a search (edge-cases §3).

In Sell it, a typed price more than 3 times the top of the sold range, or under a third of the bottom, asks once with the range on the sheet, and the button says the price it will use; the next tap makes the draft. A price inside the range asks nothing (edge-cases §3).
